hints: Notice the original length is $L_0$ and the stretched length is $L_1$, so first write the extension $L_1-L_0$.
Recall strain is extension divided by original length, so divide that extension by $L_0$.
Split the fraction $(L_1-L_0)/L_0$ into two terms and compare with the $L_1/L_0$ forms in the options.
walkthrough: Identify the given lengths: original length $= L_0$ and final length $= L_1$.
State the definition of tensile strain: $strain = extension / original length$.
Write the extension as final length minus original length: $x = L_1 - L_0$.

options.A: Strain equals extension divided by original length, so $(L_1-L_0)/L_0 = L_1/L_0 - 1$, which is dimensionless as required.
options.B: $L_1-L_0$ is the extension $x$ of the wire, not the strain, and it still has units of length.
options.C: Adding 1 gives $(L_1+L_0)/L_0$, which is larger than the fractional increase in length.
options.D: $L_1+L_0$ is the sum of the lengths, not the change in length, and it has units of length.
